newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian trade seeks crude edible oil imports.
newsitem.headline: Indian trade seeks crude edible oil imports.

text.p: India's edible oil trade on Thursday urged the government to cut customs duty on unrefined edible oil to encourage imports and activate the country's idle refining capacity.
Industry officials said currently refined and unrefined edible oil carry uniform 20 percent import duty.

"The government should see that import duty on refined edible oil is more than crude oil to encourage crude edible oil imports," B.V. Mehta, executive director of the Bombay-based Solvent Extractors' Association of India, told Reuters.
"The duty differential will help inflow of crude edible oil which would help augment our idle refining capacity."
Industry officials said low global edible oil prices had tempted Indian importers to make heavy commitments, mainly palm olein from Malaysia, leading to a sharp fall in domestic edible oil prices.

Prices of Palm oil in the Malaysian market had been showing a downward trend due to rising output and expectation of higher stocks. On Thursday, the September futures contract was down 11 ringgit at 1,126 ringgit ($450.76) a tonne.
In refined palm oil, July RBD palm oil was offered at $495 a tonne FOB Malaysia, Aug/Sep at $490 and Oct/Nov/Dec at $490. July RBD palm olein saw offers at $527.50.
"The Indian market is flooded with imports," said O.P. Goenka, a senior official at the Central Organisation for Oil Industry and Trade.
"About 40,000 tonnes of imported oil are arriving every week at the Indian ports," Mehta said.
Trade officials said India imported about 900,000 tonnes of edible oil between November and June. Another 600,000 tonnes are expected to arrive between July and October.
India imported 1.25 million tonnes of edible oil in 1995/96 (November-October).

Industry officials said a sharp rise in imports had depressed domestic edible oil prices by about 2,000 rupees per tonne in the past one month, raising the possibility that oilseed farmers would shift to other crops.
"The government and consumers are happy because inflation is under control, but farmers are unhappy as edible oil prices are steadily falling," Mehta said.
"The falling prices may force farmers to shift to other crops," Goenka said.
Dealers said palm olein oil was quoted at 26,000 rupees per tonne in the domestic markets and sunflower (crude) was quoted at 27,000 tonnes, about the same as last week.
They said imported palm olein oil was quoted at $560 per tonne C & F, and imported sunflower oil (crude) from Argentina was quoted at $570-575 per tonne C & F.
"One reason for domestic prices to be down is that Malaysian palm oil crop is expected to be about 10 percent higher than last year," Goenka said.
Traders said the prices were expected to remain depressed until end-August due to dull domestic demand.
"For another two months, prices will remain depressed," said C.M. Amla, a leading New Delhi edible oil dealer. "Fresh demand will come after August when festival season starts."
During the Hindu festival months of September to November, demand for edible oil shoots up and domestic supplies dry up.
